key_insight: Combine reasoning over heterogeneous, cross-domain user signals with knowledge distillation (and reinforcement learning) to infer deep, reusable user interests and compress that reasoning into a lightweight model for scalable news recommendation.
problem_solved: How to move beyond surface-level click behavior to recover underlying, transferable user interests from heterogeneous signals while keeping inference fast and scalable for production systems.
method: A reasoning (teacher) module that integrates cross-domain signals to infer latent user interests—trained with reinforcement learning to optimize long-term recommendation objectives.
Knowledge distillation that transfers the teacher's reasoning into a compact student model for low-latency serving.
Joint training/optimization that balances recommendation effectiveness with model size and serving efficiency for large-scale deployment.
impact: Enables practitioners to deploy more personalized, generalizable news recommendation systems that capture deeper user intents without incurring high inference cost—improving relevance while meeting production latency and resource constraints.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram showing teacher (reasoning + RL) → distillation → student (production) pipeline
Flowchart of heterogeneous cross-domain signals (news, search, clicks, preferences) being fused into latent interest vectors
Bar/line chart comparing recommendation quality vs. inference latency or model size (teacher vs. student)
t-SNE/UMAP visualization of learned user-interest embeddings to show clustering and transferability
paper_title: Learning User Interests via Reasoning and Distillation for Cross-Domain News Recommendation
paper_authors: Mengdan Zhu, Yufan Zhao, Tao Di, Yulan Yan, Liang Zhao
